beats.text: Traditional 3D scans can look complete while missing the instant an accessible route breaks. One lift closes, and the expected journey disappears.
SceneIndex adds persistent meaning beneath the Gaussian splat: rooms, gates, lifts, routes, and evidence that people and agents share.
The mission: reach Platform 2 from Entrance A without stairs, while exposing uncertainty. The agent reads the camera and finds the accessible gate.
The first route uses the east corridor and Lift 1. It appears in the scene, where every turn stays inspectable.
Then Lift 1 closes. Its proxy turns red, its state changes, and the route fails visibly. The outage is reversible, never hidden.
The agent reroutes through Lift 2. The trip remains possible, but the West corridor raises a warning: wayfinding readiness is only just over half.
Why? The directional sign has one oblique, low resolution view. Connectivity is known, but its text remains unverified.
SceneIndex turns doubt into fieldwork: recapture the sign front-on, then walk a reverse pass from Lift 2. Six markers make the plan concrete.
The person keeps control: inspect, challenge, accept, or undo. One action restores Lift 1 and the clean baseline.
Web M C P connects to this live interface. Ten narrow tools share scene state, validation, effects, and a human-visible action timeline.
The station is synthetic, but this pattern supports accessibility review, handover, inspection, maintenance, and targeted recapture without pretending pixels know more.
SceneIndex makes a place searchable, testable, and honest about evidence. When the world changes, the route changes with it.
